bug_semantics: The MCP approval-request entry point accepts caller-controlled categoryName and passes it unchanged to ApprovalStorage.createApproval(). That method formed categoryDir with join(this.approvalsDir, categoryName), recursively created the resulting directory, and wrote the approval JSON beneath it. A categoryName containing parent-directory components and directory separators could therefore normalize outside .spec-workflow/approvals and cause a local caller to create or overwrite an approval JSON outside the intended storage tree.
flaw_origin: The repository's root commit introduced the complete vulnerable path in one public commit: request-approval exposed categoryName in the MCP input schema and forwarded args.categoryName to createApproval, while createApproval used the value as a filesystem path component without validation or a containment check before mkdir and writeFile. Later refactors preserved that mechanism; they did not originate it.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object identifies author Pimzino <jose@freitasuk.com> and committer Pimzino <jose@freitasuk.com>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/Pimzino/spec-workflow-mcp/issues/220 reproduces on 2.2.6 with categoryName=..\..\..\spec-workflow-poc-outside and identifies the flow src/tools/approvals.ts -> ApprovalStorage.createApproval() -> join(this.approvalsDir, categoryName) -> fs.writeFile().

git show b66281c495aa93e58da69c9227ac5506c16d0ca4:src/tools/request-approval.ts shows that the root commit's MCP schema accepted categoryName and requestApprovalHandler passed args.categoryName directly to approvalStorage.createApproval().

git show b66281c495aa93e58da69c9227ac5506c16d0ca4:src/dashboard/approval-storage.ts shows createApproval constructing const categoryDir = join(this.approvalsDir, categoryName), calling fs.mkdir(categoryDir, { recursive: true }), then writing join(categoryDir, `${id}.json`) without categoryName validation or containment enforcement.

git blame -L 259,304 d71a301d9ecfe4f603d3b48c88240de82a066b99 -- src/dashboard/approval-storage.ts attributes the createApproval signature, categoryName storage, unsafe categoryDir join, mkdir, and writeFile lines to b66281c495aa93e58da69c9227ac5506c16d0ca4; git log -S'.createApproval(' also reaches that root commit for the original caller/sink path.

git rev-list --parents -n 1 b66281c495aa93e58da69c9227ac5506c16d0ca4 outputs only the commit itself, proving it is the repository root and has no immediate parent tree. Thus introducer_parent is necessarily null and the vulnerable path is absent from the empty prehistory immediately before the root commit; no public squash members exist to decompose.

Version-boundary checks: package.json is 0.0.1 at the BIC, 2.2.6 at 1b7ae69032e8083663d0814ff54f1f4f644868b1, and 2.2.7 at 9c7a7839e690bb4543f0e7481b5740d23808e5fe. git merge-base of the BIC and the 2.2.6 release commit returns the BIC, while git merge-base of the 2.2.6 release commit and the fix returns 1b7ae69032e8083663d0814ff54f1f4f644868b1, establishing that the vulnerable mechanism predates 2.2.6 and the fix is the 2.2.7 boundary.

The advisory names 9c7a7839e690bb4543f0e7481b5740d23808e5fe as the patch, and first-party PR https://github.com/Pimzino/spec-workflow-mcp/pull/222 describes the same traversal. The commit changes version 2.2.6 to 2.2.7, validates categoryName at the tool and storage boundaries, and replaces the vulnerable raw category-directory join with PathUtils.safeJoin(); its sole parent d71a301d9ecfe4f603d3b48c88240de82a066b99 still contains the vulnerable join.

BIC-only AI check: git show -s --format='%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>|%B' b66281c495aa93e58da69c9227ac5506c16d0ca4 reports human author/committer Pimzino <jose@freitasuk.com> and a release-note message with no AI attribution trailer.
reasoning: The vulnerability is an untrusted-path-to-filesystem-sink error, not merely a missing check added by the patch. The root commit is the smallest public BIC because it first wrote both the externally supplied categoryName flow and the unsafe join/mkdir/writeFile sink; line history confirms the vulnerable sink survived from that commit through the direct pre-fix parent. The BIC has no parent, so parent absence was verified by the root commit's empty parent list rather than by naming a nonexistent SHA, and there is no reachable earlier member history to decompose. The BIC is ancestral to the 2.2.6 release, and the advisory's direct repair is the commit that changes the package to 2.2.7 and blocks or contains category paths. Finally, attribution is based only on the BIC commit object: it has a human author and committer and no AI marker, so the causal result is NOT_AI.
